cards.name: Neutral Density 20
cards.summary: Black overlay that fades out to the right: opacity 20% at the left edge down to 0% at the right edge (a plain two-stop fade); the colour is black (stored as HSB 0/0/0 or #000000) all the way. The darkest it ever gets is 20% black, never solid. PGD's thumbnail shows it on its own over a checkerboard: about 20% black at the left edge, 10% at the middle and 0% at the right edge. The number in the name is the starting opacity (20%): a straight fade.
use_for: darken a bright sky or one side of a photo like a graduated neutral-density filter (rotate or Reverse so the dark end sits where you want it)
scrim behind white headline text on a busy photo, dark end under the text
directional shadow or vignette edge on a poster or thumbnail
avoid: it never gets darker than 20% black, so it cannot make a solid dark panel; use Black To Transparent or Foreground to Transparent with a black foreground for 100% at one end
it adds no colour and slightly greys saturated skies; for a coloured sunset sky add a warm or blue gradient layer in Soft Light or Multiply (inferred)
cards.applies_to: a Gradient Fill layer over a photo or artwork (Layer > New Fill Layer > Gradient), best with the layer's blend mode left on Normal and the opacity stops doing the work; also the Gradient tool on a layer mask, or a Gradient Overlay effect. Angle and Reverse are set where it is applied; the thumbnail is angle 0 with the dark end at the left.
cards.how_to_apply: Not in the Gradients panel's default list (the harvest did not find it in the live preset list). Load the library <Photoshop 2026 install folder>/Required/Legacy Gradients.grd (Gradient Editor > Load..., or the Gradients panel menu > Import Gradients...; neither route observed by PGD); the preset sits under 'Legacy Gradients > Neutral Density'. Script: PGD rendered it by reading this preset's Grad descriptor out of that .grd (ActionDescriptor.fromStream on the file, item picked by its position) and making a Gradient Fill layer with Action Manager Make (contentLayer / gradientLayer, type linear, angle 0).

cards.summary: Dark-to-light toning ramp (7 stops), left to right from near-black (#030303) to white (#FFFFFF): shadows (15% along) dark steel blue (#15323B), midtones (50%) steel blue (#6D8390), highlights (85%) pale mauve-pink (#E0D2D6). A cool tone with a faint mauve-pink cast in the highlights meant for a Gradient Map over a black-and-white photo (it maps shadows to the left end and highlights to the right end).
use_for: Gradient Map adjustment layer over a black-and-white or desaturated photo for a toned-print look
vintage or darkroom-print poster photo, editorial portrait, heritage-brand imagery
duotone/tritone-style photo wash before adding type in white or black
avoid: the ends are essentially black (#030303) and white (#FFFFFF), so the toning shows only in the mid-tones and the deepest blacks and brightest whites stay neutral; if you want tinted blacks or whites this is the wrong ramp

a Gradient Map also re-maps contrast, because it assigns colours by brightness and discards the photo's own colour; set the layer to Color blend mode if only the tint should change (inferred standard practice, not tested here)
cards.applies_to: a Gradient Map adjustment layer (Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Gradient Map) over a photo or a flattened black-and-white image: shadows take the left end, highlights the right end. It also works in any other gradient slot (fills, overlays), but the dark-to-light order makes it a tonal ramp. The thumbnail is a linear fill at angle 0 with the first stop on the left.
cards.how_to_apply: Not in the Gradients panel's default list (the harvest did not find it in the live preset list). Load the library <Photoshop 2026 install folder>/Required/Legacy Gradients.grd (Gradient Editor > Load..., or the Gradients panel menu > Import Gradients...; neither route observed by PGD); the preset sits under 'Legacy Gradients > Photographic Toning'. Script: PGD rendered it by reading this preset's Grad descriptor out of that .grd (ActionDescriptor.fromStream on the file, item picked by its position) and making a Gradient Fill layer with Action Manager Make (contentLayer / gradientLayer, type linear, angle 0).
